facts.fact_text: The three applicants in the present case were involved in a number of public events in 2007-2008 in Rostov-na-Donu.
On 24 November 2007 Mr Nagibin proceeded with the static demonstration (picket).

On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold a meeting of approximately three hundred participants on Sovetov Square from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m. on 30 June 2007.

On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold the 'Dissenters' March' (Марш несогласных) along Sadovaya and Sovetskaya Streets following the meeting on Sovetov Square on 30 June 2007.
On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold another meeting at Karl Marx Square until 7.30 p.m. on 30 June 2007.
At 5.20 p.m. on 12 December 2008 Mr Nagibin came to Voroshilovskiy Drive for a solitary demonstration.
Mr Nagibin carried a sandwich board during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
Mr Nagibin distributed leaflets to passers-by during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the location of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the time of conduct of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the manner of conduct of several public events.

On 24 November 2007 Mr Nagibin was apprehended because his passport was found to be defiled with unauthorised pen writing and the police officers intended to draft the relevant record of the administrative offence at the police station.
Mr Nagibin was brought to a police station and charged with non-compliance with a lawful order of a police officer under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
On 20 June 2007 the Rostov-na-Donu town administration informed Mr Nagibin that the contemplated events had not been sufficiently prepared.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration imposed restrictions as to the location of the public event on each occasion that Mr Nikolayev submitted a notification.
On 8 December 2008 the Rostov-na-Donu town administration replied that Mr Nagibin had to hold the picket in another area, in front of the Sports Palace.
At approximately 5.40 p.m. on 12 December 2008 two police officers apprehended Mr Nagibin during his solitary demonstration at Voroshilovskiy Drive.

Mr Nagibin was charged with a breach of public order and verbal assaults, an administrative offence under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, following his apprehension on 12 December 2008.

The Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found that the police officers had acted within their competence because they had the right, under section 11 §§ 2 and 15 of the Police Act, to check the identity papers of individuals suspected of a criminal or administrative offence.

On 2 December 2007 Mr Nagibin was convicted of the administrative offence of non-compliance with a lawful order of a police officer on the basis of the police report and oral testimony of officer Mr Kh.

On 13 December 2008 the Justice of the Peace of the 6th Court Circuit of the Kirovskiy District found Mr Nagibin guilty of breach of public order and verbal assaults under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The police officers testified that they had received operative information on the preparation by National-Bolsheviks of an unlawful march in Moscow, known as the 'Dissenters' March'.
The police officers testified that they were requested to conduct explanatory and preventive discussions with prospective participants in the 'Dissenters' March', including Mr Nagibin.

The Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found that the police officers had acted within their competence because they had the right, under section 11 §§ 2 and 15 of the Police Act, to check the identity papers of individuals suspected of a criminal or administrative offence.
On 7 March 2008 the Pervomayskiy District Court found that there had been no breach of Mr Nagibin's right to hold a picket because the Rostov-na-Donu town administration had not prohibited the event.
The Pervomayskiy District Court found on 7 March 2008 that Mr Nagibin had actually begun picketing but had been detained and brought to administrative liability for an unrelated offence.

On 8 October 2007 the Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found in favour of Mr Nagibin, Mr Batyy and Mr Ye. regarding the Rostov-na-Donu town administration's de facto refusal of their application to hold a march.
On 30 June 2010 the Supreme Court of Russia, following a request by the Ombudsman, held that the replies of the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of 8 and 10 December 2008 were unlawful.
